import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/training_3.csv"
]

# Read all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
dfs = [pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0) for path in source_files]

# According to operation_history, perform UNION of all source tables
# All source tables have the same schema ['WarNum', 'TransTo']
# The target schema is ['WarNum': integer, 'TransTo': integer]
# The source data has NaN in 'TransTo', we need to convert 'TransTo' to integer type.
# Since NaN cannot be converted directly to int, fill NaN with 0 as in target examples.

for df in dfs:
    # Fill NaN in 'TransTo' with 0
    df['TransTo'] = df['TransTo'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    # Ensure 'WarNum' is integer type as well
    df['WarNum'] = df['WarNum'].astype(int)

# Concatenate all dataframes (UNION)
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure the final dataframe columns and types match the target schema
target_df = target_df[['WarNum', 'TransTo']]
target_df['WarNum'] = target_df['WarNum'].astype(int)
target_df['TransTo'] = target_df['TransTo'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the specified path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Rename TransTo columns to keep them distinct after join
source0 = source0.rename(columns={"TransTo": "TransTo_Source4_58_0"})
source1 = source1.rename(columns={"TransTo": "TransTo_Source4_58_1"})
source2 = source2.rename(columns={"TransTo": "TransTo_Source4_58_2"})
source3 = source3.rename(columns={"TransTo": "TransTo_Source4_58_3"})

# Join source0 and source1 on WarNum (inner join)
join_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="WarNum", how="inner")

# Join source2 and source3 on WarNum (inner join)
join_23 = pd.merge(source2, source3, on="WarNum", how="inner")

# Join the two joined tables on WarNum (inner join)
joined_all = pd.merge(join_01, join_23, on="WarNum", how="inner")

# Aggregate: group by WarNum, take max of each TransTo column (to convert NaN to 0 or 1)
# Since TransTo columns contain NaN and 0,1, max will pick 1 if exists, else 0
agg = joined_all.groupby("WarNum", as_index=False).agg({
    "TransTo_Source4_58_0": "max",
    "TransTo_Source4_58_1": "max",
    "TransTo_Source4_58_2": "max",
    "TransTo_Source4_58_3": "max"
})

# Now, the target schema is ['WarNum', 'TransTo'] with TransTo as integer
# The target examples show TransTo as a single integer column, but sources have multiple TransTo columns
# We need to combine these TransTo columns into a single TransTo column
# Since FD says WarNum -> TransTo, and target has one TransTo per WarNum,
# we can combine by taking max across all TransTo columns per WarNum

agg["TransTo"] = agg[[
    "TransTo_Source4_58_0",
    "TransTo_Source4_58_1",
    "TransTo_Source4_58_2",
    "TransTo_Source4_58_3"
]].max(axis=1).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Select only WarNum and TransTo columns for final output
final_df = agg[["WarNum", "TransTo"]]

# Write to target file
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_58/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
